common_name: Tarka Agapanthus (Late-Blooming Mauve Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in sun, well-drained soil enriched with humus; Tarka was raised by UK Agapanthus National Collection holder Dick Fulcher and is valued for its unusually late, mauve-toned flowers.

directions: Tarka produces large, full rounded heads of pale violet-mauve flowers with a darker midrib on each tepal, distinguishing it from the many blue-shaded agapanthus cultivars. It flowers later than most, typically from late August into October, extending the agapanthus season into autumn. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil with added humus, and avoid dividing established clumps too often since flowering improves when slightly congested. Mulch the crown over winter in colder parts of its range.

common_name: Hoyland Chelsea Blue Agapanthus (Dark Blue-Purple Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in a south- or west-facing full-sun position; raised by Hoyland Plant Centre, UK National Collection holders for Agapanthus.

directions: Hoyland Chelsea Blue forms clumps of strap-shaped evergreen leaves topped by rounded heads of dark blue-purple, tubular flowers held on strong stems through summer. It needs a sheltered, sunny spot and benefits from winter protection in cold-winter gardens since it is only half-hardy. Keep soil on the drier side once established, as agapanthus flower best when their roots are slightly restricted. Deadhead spent flower stems at the base to tidy the clump.

common_name: Yorkshire Rose Agapanthus (White Lily of the Nile with Pink Flecks)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; a compact Hoyland Plant Centre introduction bred for its unusual flecked flower coloring.

directions: Yorkshire Rose bears rounded clusters of predominantly white flowers accented with pink flecks on the petal bases, giving the flower heads a subtle blush when viewed up close. Its compact habit and erect stems to about 20 inches make it well suited to large containers as well as border fronts. It is deciduous, dying back fully in winter, which contributes to its good cold hardiness compared with evergreen agapanthus types. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil and avoid overwatering.

common_name: Windsor Grey Agapanthus (Pale Lavender-Grey Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; valued among UK growers for its unusual, subtle flower coloring.

directions: Windsor Grey is prized for its unusual, muted flower color, a shade between palest lavender and soft grey, with faint green tints from the pollen and the green-based florets. The effect is a subtler, more smoky counterpoint to the typical bold blues and whites of most agapanthus. Flowers appear from midsummer into early autumn above clumps of strap-shaped deciduous foliage. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil and let clumps become slightly congested for best flowering.

common_name: Timaru Agapanthus (Deep Violet-Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; a semi-evergreen, medium-height cultivar named for the New Zealand town.

directions: Timaru carries strong, upright stems topped with large, near-spherical umbels of deep violet-blue, tubular flowers up to six inches across, held well above clumps of strap-shaped, semi-evergreen foliage. It flowers reliably through summer and makes a bold architectural statement in a mixed border or large container. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil and divide only when flowering begins to decline, since agapanthus bloom best when their roots are slightly crowded.

common_name: Oxford Blue Agapanthus (Compact Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; a compact, cold-hardy selection of Agapanthus campanulatus.

directions: Oxford Blue forms a compact clump of narrow, strap-shaped, mid-green deciduous foliage reaching about a foot tall, with hemispherical heads of blue, funnel-shaped flowers held on straight stems well above the leaves in late summer. Its smaller stature compared to many agapanthus cultivars makes it a good fit for border fronts and container displays. As a deciduous campanulatus selection it dies back to the crown each winter, contributing to strong cold hardiness. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil.

common_name: Summer Heat Peruvian Lily (Fire-Engine Red Alstroemeria with Yellow Flare)

planting.note: Plant container-grown roots in spring in moderately moist, well-drained soil in full sun; a Proven Winners Perennials introduction bred for garden hardiness.

directions: Summer Heat bears large, fire-engine red flowers with a bright yellow central flare speckled across the petals, resembling flickering campfire flames on tall, sturdy stems. It blooms from midsummer into fall and is later to emerge in spring than most garden perennials, then grows quickly to catch up. Flowers are excellent and long-lasting when cut; pulling spent stems from the base rather than cutting them encourages faster rebloom. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil with consistent moisture.

common_name: Summer Breeze Peruvian Lily (Peach and Apricot Alstroemeria)

planting.note: Plant container-grown roots in spring in moderately moist, well-drained soil in full sun; a patented Dutch-bred Proven Winners Perennials introduction arising as a branch mutation of an earlier potted alstroemeria cultivar.

directions: Summer Breeze produces flowers with sunny yellow centers fading into peach petals with apricot-toned backs, set off by dark-tinted, purple-black foliage that contrasts attractively with the warm bloom color. It flowers continuously from summer into fall and holds up well as a cut flower. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil with even moisture, and mulch over winter in the colder end of its hardiness range.

planting.note: Plant container-grown roots in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; a Proven Winners Perennials introduction in the Summer Paradise series, cold hardy to Zone 6 with winter protection.

directions: Summer Break is a floriferous, large-flowered selection with creamy-white petals boldly edged in pink, warm yellow centers, and dark brown speckled detailing. It produces an abundance of consistently shaped blooms through mid to late summer, giving it strong landscape presence as well as florist-quality cut flowers that hold up well after cutting. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil, and provide winter mulch at the colder end of its hardiness range.

common_name: Inticancha Sunstar Peruvian Lily (Compact Fuchsia-Pink Patio Alstroemeria)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; part of the dwarf Inticancha patio series bred for container and border use.

directions: Inticancha Sunstar forms a compact, bushy clump of narrow, dark green, tropical-looking leaves topped with fuchsia-pink flowers whose yellow throats are speckled with deep red. Unlike many alstroemeria it stays dwarf, with flowering stems to about a foot, making it well suited to containers and patio pots. It is notably resilient to high summer heat compared with other Inticancha series varieties, flowering heavily from early summer well into fall. Deadhead or pull spent stems from the base to encourage continuous reflush.
